summary: 连续作决定可能使人转向省力、短视的选择。文章以购物实验和补充葡萄糖的研究说明“决策疲劳”假说，也呈现对其生理机制的质疑，最后讨论怎样安排重要决定。

paragraphs.brief: 无论人们多么理性，他们都无法在决定后做出决策，不付出生物代价。
sentences: No matter how rational people try to be, they can’t make decision after decision without paying a biological price.
无论人们多么理性，他们都无法在决定后做出决策，不付出生物代价。
This ‘decision fatigue’ is different from ordinary physical fatigue.
这种“决定疲劳症”不同于普通的身体疲劳症。
People are not conscious of being tired, but nevertheless they are low on energy.
人们并不感到疲惫，但是他们却缺乏能量。

The more choices one makes throughout the day, the harder it becomes for the brain, and eventually it looks for shortcuts: either to act impulsively instead of expending the energy to think through the possible results, or the ultimate energy saver: do nothing.
一天作出越多选择，大脑就越难选择，最终寻找捷径：要么是冲动地行动，要么是将精力花在思考可能的结果上，要么是最终的节能者：什么都不做。
Avoiding a decision often creates bigger problems in the long run, but for the moment it eases the mental strain.
从长远来看，避免作出决定往往会造成更大的问题，但目前它缓解了精神紧张。

paragraphs.brief: 决定疲劳症涉及一种被称为自我耗竭的现象，这是社会心理学家Roy F. Baumeister所创造的术语。
sentences: Decision fatigue involves a phenomenon called ego depletion, a term coined by social psychologist Roy F. Baumeister.
决定疲劳症涉及一种被称为自我耗竭的现象，这是社会心理学家Roy F. Baumeister所创造的术语。
His research demonstrated that there is a finite store of mental stamina for exerting self-control.
他的研究表明，在自我控制方面，精神上的耐力有限。
For example, when people fended off the temptation to eat freshly baked biscuits, they were then less able to resist other temptations.
例如，当人们摆脱吃新鲜烤饼干的诱惑时，他们就更没有能力抵抗其他诱惑。
When they tried to resist the urge to cry during a sad movie, afterwards they gave up more quickly on tasks requiring self-discipline, such as working on a geometry puzzle.
当他们试图抵制悲伤的电影中哭泣的冲动时，后来他们更快地放弃了需要自律的任务，例如，在几何拼图上工作。
The experiments confirmed the 19th-century notion of willpower being like a muscle that became tired with use; something which could be conserved by avoiding temptation.
实验证实了19世纪的意志力概念就像是肌肉疲惫的用法避免诱惑可以保护它

paragraphs.brief: 正如Jonathan Levav所展示的，决策疲劳使人们很容易被那些知道如何计时销售的市场人士所左右。
sentences: Decision fatigue leaves people vulnerable to marketers who know how to time their sales, as Jonathan Levav demonstrated.
正如Jonathan Levav所展示的，决策疲劳使人们很容易被那些知道如何计时销售的市场人士所左右。
He visited a tailor to have a suit made for his wedding and began going through the choices of fabric, buttons, and so forth, and when he got through the third pile of fabric samples.
他拜访了一位裁缝准备为他的婚礼准备一件西装并开始研究布料、纽扣等的选择以及他穿过第三堆布料样本时的选择
Levav recalls, “I couldn’t tell the choices apart anymore.
莱夫夫回忆道，“我再也不能分辨这些选择了。
After a while my only response to the tailor became, ‘What do you recommend?’”
我对裁缝的唯一反应是："你建议什么？"

Levav put the experience to use in an experiment conducted at German car dealerships, where real customers had to choose among four styles of gearshift knobs, 25 configurations of the engine and gearbox, and a palette of 56 colours for the interior.
Levav将经验用于在德国汽车经销商进行的一项实验中，在试验中，真正的顾客不得不选择四个轮椅式把手、25个发动机和变速箱配置以及一个56种颜色的内部调色板。
As they started picking features, customers would carefully weigh the choices, but as decision fatigue set in they would start settling for the default option.
随着客户开始选择特征，他们将仔细权衡选择，但随着决定疲劳症的出现，他们将开始为默认选项进行结算。
By manipulating the order of the car buyers’ choices, the researchers found that customers would end up paying more.
研究者们通过操纵汽车购买者选择的顺序，发现顾客最终会支付更多的钱。

paragraphs.brief: 同样，在大多数超市，现金登记簿上也突出提到甜点。
sentences: Similarly, sweet snacks are featured prominently at cash registers at most supermarkets.
同样，在大多数超市，现金登记簿上也突出提到甜点。
With their willpower reduced after shopping, people are especially vulnerable to sweet drinks and snacks.
由于购物后意志力减弱，人们特别容易受到甜饮和零食的伤害。
While supermarkets figured this out a long time ago, only recently did researchers discover why.
虽然超市很久以前就发现了但最近研究人员才发现了原因
Baumeister’s research team tested the notion that people could build up willpower by first indulging in pleasure.
Baumeister的研究团队测试了人们可以通过先沉溺于快乐来建立意志力的概念。
They found that a delicious, thick milkshake strengthened willpower by helping people perform better than expected on their next task.
他们发现一个美味而厚厚的奶昔增强了意志力帮助人们完成下一个任务
However, the experiment also included a control group who drank a tasteless low-fat dairy beverage.
然而，该试验还包括一个控制小组，他喝了一种无品低脂乳品饮料。
It provided them with no pleasure, yet it produced similar improvements in self-control.
它不让他们高兴，但却在自我控制方面产生了类似的改进。

Baumeister concluded that even the tasteless drink had worked because the brain, like the rest of the body, derived energy from glucose, the simple sugar manufactured from all kinds of foods, including milk.
Baumeister的结论是，即使没有品味的饮料也起作用了，因为大脑与身体的其余部分一样，从包括牛奶在内的各种食物中制造的简单的糖糖中产生能量。

paragraphs.brief: 为了确定原因和效果，Baumeister实验室的研究人员尝试在涉及柠檬汁与糖或甜食混合的实验中给大脑加油。
sentences: To establish cause and effect, researchers at Baumeister’s lab tried refueling the brain in experiments involving lemonade mixed either with sugar or with a diet sweetener.
为了确定原因和效果，Baumeister实验室的研究人员尝试在涉及柠檬汁与糖或甜食混合的实验中给大脑加油。
The sugary lemonade provided a burst of glucose, the effects of which could be observed immediately in the lab; the sugarless sweeteners tasted similar but did not contain the glucose.
甘蔗柠檬汁提供了一股葡萄糖，其影响可在实验室立即观察到；无糖糖糖的味道相似，但不含葡萄糖。
Again and again, the sugar restored willpower, but the artificial sweetener had no effect.
糖一次又一次地恢复了意志力但人工糖却毫无作用

The glucose would mitigate the ego depletion and sometimes completely reverse it, improving self-control and the quality of decisions: the subjects resisted irrational bias when making choices and, when making financial decisions, they were more likely to choose the better long-term strategy instead of going for a quick payoff.
葡萄糖可以减轻自我耗竭，有时可以完全扭转这种耗竭，提高自我控制和决定的质量：主体在做出选择时抵制非理性的偏见，在做出财务决定时，他们更有可能选择更好的长期战略，而不是快速回报。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，一些脑部研究者对葡萄糖的连接有保留。
sentences: However, some brain researchers had reservations about the glucose connection.
然而，一些脑部研究者对葡萄糖的连接有保留。
“Todd Heatherton, a pioneer of social neuroscience, believed in ego depletion but didn’t see how this process could be caused simply by variations in glucose levels.”
“Tord Heatherton是社会神经科学的先锋，他相信自我枯竭，但不明白这个过程是如何仅仅由葡萄糖水平的变化引起的。
To observe the process, and to see if it could be reversed by glucose, Heatherton’s team recorded images of the brains of 45 people who were on a low-calorie diet as they reacted to pictures of food.
为了观察这个过程，并且看看它能否被葡萄糖扭转过来，Heatherton的团队记录了45人脑部的图像，他们正在低卡路里饮食，因为他们对食物图片的反应。
Next, these dieters watched a comedy video while forcing themselves to suppress their laughter—thereby draining mental energy and inducing ego depletion.
接下来，这些饮食者观看了喜剧视频，同时强迫自己抑制他们的笑声，从而耗尽了精神能量，并导致自我耗竭。
When they were again shown pictures of food, further brain scans revealed more activity in the brain’s reward centre and a decrease in the amygdala, which helps control impulses.
当他们再次被展示食物照片时，进一步的脑扫描揭示了大脑奖赏中心的更多活动以及阿米格达拉的减少，这有助于控制冲动。
The food’s appeal, in other words, registered more strongly while impulse control weakened.
换句话说，食品的吸引力在冲动控制减弱的同时更加强烈。
What surprised Heatherton was that administering glucose completely reversed the brain changes brought about by ego depletion.
海瑟顿很惊讶的是葡萄糖的服用完全扭转了自我耗竭带来的大脑变化

paragraphs.brief: Baumeister说，“良好的决策不是人的特征。
sentences: “Good decision-making is not a trait of the person,” Baumeister says.
Baumeister说，“良好的决策不是人的特征。
“It’s a state that fluctuates.”
”“这是一个波动性国家。
His studies show that people with the best self-control are the ones who avoid temptations, and who establish habits that eliminate the mental effort of making choices.
他的研究显示，有最佳自我控制的人是那些避免诱惑的人，他们建立习惯，消除作出选择的心理努力。
Instead of counting on willpower all day, they conserve it so that it’s available for important decisions.
他们不会指望整天的意志力，而是保护意志力，以便它能够用于重要的决策。
“Even the wisest people won’t make good choices when they’re not rested and their glucose is low,” Baumeister notes.
鲍米斯特的笔记：“即使最聪明的人也不会做出正确的选择当他们不休息和他们的葡萄糖低。”
If a decision must be made late in the afternoon or in the evening, they know not to do it on an empty stomach.
如果决定必须在下午或晚上作出，他们知道不能空着肚子这样做。
The best decision-makers, according to Baumeister, “are the ones who know when not to trust themselves.”
Baumeister认为，最好的决策者是“知道何时不信任自己的人”。

items.en: research in which two substances that tasted alike had different effects on the subjects
items.zh: 研究中两种同味物质对研究对象产生不同影响
items.why: 题干中的“两种味道相似的物质对应“sugary lemonade”和“sugarless sweeteners”, “tasted similar”。“不同的影响对应前者 restored willpower,后者hada no effect。这一点只在E段出现，所以答案是 E。

items.en: an instance where controlling emotions while viewing something upsetting led to a lack of perseverance in other activities
items.zh: 在一个例子中，控制情绪同时又看到一些令人沮丧的东西导致在其他活动中缺乏毅力
items.why: 受试者看悲伤电影时忍住眼泪，之后做需自律的几何任务更快放弃，显示先前控制情绪影响坚持。

items.en: an explanation of why it is important to eat something before making a decision at the end of the day
items.zh: 解释为什么在一天结束前一定要吃点东西
items.why: 题干问“为什么重要”,答案就是: 血糖低会影响决策质量，所以要先吃点东西，这个因果解释正是 G 段这两句，因此选 G。

items.en: a reference to a researcher who was not initially convinced of the effect of glucose
items.zh: 提到一个研究者起初不相信葡萄糖的影响
items.why: 希瑟顿接受自我损耗的概念，但起初不相信它能仅由葡萄糖水平变化解释。

items.en: an account of research that mirrored an experience the researcher had in his personal life
items.zh: 研究的描述反映了研究人员在个人生活中的经历
items.why: 先讲 Levav 自己在裁缝店被选项“搞晕” 的个人经历，然后说他“把这次经历用在实验中”,就是题干“mirrored an experience…in his personal life” 的意思。所以答案是 C。

items.en: an example of how the location of products in a shop can be used to take advantage of ‘decision fatigue’
items.zh: 说明如何利用商店产品的位置来利用“决定疲劳症”的例子
items.why: 购物后意志力下降，甜食和饮料更有诱惑；把它们摆在结账处就是利用这种决策疲劳。

items.en: The biological price of decision-making Even when people attempt to be ________, they experience ‘decision fatigue’ if they make several decisions in a row.
items.zh: 即使人们努力保持________，连续作出几个决定后也会出现“决策疲劳”。
items.why: 摘要里的“attempt to be…” 直接对应原文“try to be…”,唯一可填的描述是 rationa/。词形也保持原样，故答案为 rational。

items.en: They are not aware of how ________ they are, but it is increasingly more difficult for their brains to make decisions as the day progresses.
items.zh: 他们并未察觉自己有多________，但一天之中，越往后，大脑作决定就越吃力。
items.why: 摘要中“not aware of"=原文“not conscious of,后面缺的词就是太eq。而且必须是一个词，所以填 tired。

items.en: After making many decisions in one day, the brain seeks ________ in order to conserve energy.
items.zh: 一天内作出许多决定后，大脑会寻找________来节省精力。
items.why: 摘要里的“seeks…in order to conserve energy”就是对“looks for shortcuts / energy saver”的概括。名词只能填 shortcuts (注意原文也是复数),因此答案为 shortcuts。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: The energy people have for exercising willpower is limited.
items.zh: 人们行使意志力的能量是有限的。

items.en: Even an unpleasant substance had a positive effect on willpower.
items.zh: 即使是不愉快的物质也会对意志力产生积极影响。

items.en: People’s responses to images changed after having to exercise self-control.
items.zh: 人民对图像的反应在不得不自我控制后发生了变化。

items.en: The sequence of options presented to consumers could be used to the consumers’ disadvantage.
items.zh: 向消费者提出的选择的顺序可以用来使消费者处于不利地位。

pairs: had a positive effect on willpower
提高意志力／增强自制力
order of the car buyers’ choices
customers would end up paying more
让消费者吃亏，具体后果是多付钱
points: 希瑟顿接受自我损耗的概念，但起初不相信它能仅由葡萄糖水平变化解释。
摘要里的“seeks…in order to conserve energy”就是对“looks for shortcuts / energy saver”的概括。名词只能填 shortcuts (注意原文也是复数),因此答案为 shortcuts。
clauses: “that there is a finite store of mental stamina for exerting self-control”补足 demonstrated 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 demonstrated 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
…, only recently did researchers discover why.
连接词 while 引出“While supermarkets figured this out a long time ago”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: ‘Decision fatigue’ helps explain why ordinarily sensible people avoid making decisions or are easily persuaded to make the wrong decisions when they are tired.
“决定疲劳症”有助于解释为什么通常明智的人在疲劳时避免作出决定，或很容易说服他们作出错误的决定。
Yet few people are conscious of it, and researchers are only beginning to understand why it happens.
然而，很少有人意识到这一点，而研究人员才刚刚开始理解为什么会发生这种情况。
